claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your circumstances against the official Child Benefit eligibility rules, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**Key Issue:** Alex does not live with you, and your financial contribution is insufficient.

According to the official guidance, when a child doesn't live with you, you can still qualify for Child Benefit if you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep (including clothes, food, pocket money, etc.).

Currently:
- **Your weekly contribution:** £20.00
- **Child Benefit rate required:** £25.60 per week (for the eldest/only child)

Since your weekly contribution of £20.00 is less than the Child Benefit payment amount of £25.60, you don't meet the minimum contribution requirement.

**What you could do:**
If you increase your weekly contributions to at least £25.60 (or the equivalent amount) towards Alex's upkeep, you could become eligible for Child Benefit. The contributions can be made weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum to cover a set period, and they include things like clothes, food, pocket money, and financial contributions for accommodation.

reasonings:
According to the official guidance on child benefit eligibility when a child lives with someone else, the claimant needs to meet specific contribution requirements. While you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK, the rules state that you'll usually be responsible if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after them.

For a child not living with you, you can continue to get Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks if you contribute to the child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment. Your contribution of £20.00 per week falls short of the current Child Benefit rate. The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child (and £16.95 for additional children). 

Since your weekly contribution of £20.00 is less than the Child Benefit payment amount of £25.60, you do not meet the minimum contribution requirement to qualify for Child Benefit for Alex who does not live with you. Therefore, you are ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
